newsitem.title: UK: Baker resumes Western Sahara talks.
newsitem.headline: Baker resumes Western Sahara talks.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker resumed talks with Morocco and its Western Sahara foes, the Polisario Front, with a weekend meeting in London, UN officials said on Sunday.

The United Nations has been trying to organise a referendum to decide whether Western Sahara should be incorporated into Morocco, which controls most of the former Spanish colony, or become independent.

Asked for a progress report on the latest round of talks, a UN official said: "The fact that the talks have proceeded all day yesterday and today is a good sign in itself." But he would not be more specific, saying that Baker planned to make a brief statement when the London talks are wrapped up.
The two sides first met face to face last month in Lisbon under Baker's auspices.

Baker told them then that they needed to return home to consult with political leaders after he put forward "bridging proposals" aimed at ending a dispute that has been rumbling on since Spain abandoned the mineral-rich territory in 1976.
Algheria and Mauritania are attending the talks as observers.

Baker has been asked by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to recommend whether the U.N. peace plan calling for a referendum can be carried out or whether agreed adjustments could be made or other means found to resolve the dispute.
The ballot was orirginally set for January 1992 but has been repeatedly postponed because of continuing disagreements between Rabat and the Polisario Front.
